name: Databases
description: ER modelling, the relational model, relational algebra and SQL, normalisation, transactions and indexing.

nodes.name: ER model
nodes.desc: Entities, attributes, relationships, cardinality and participation constraints.
nodes.summary: You will be able to model a domain with entities, attributes and relationships and specify cardinality and participation constraints.
topics: Simple, composite, multivalued and derived attributes

nodes.name: ER to tables
nodes.desc: Mapping entities, weak entities, relationships and multivalued attributes to the fewest relations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to map an ER diagram to the minimum number of relations, handling weak entities, relationships and multivalued attributes.

nodes.name: Relational model
nodes.desc: Relations as sets of tuples, schemas, and referential integrity through foreign keys.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe relations as sets of tuples with schemas and enforce referential integrity with foreign keys.

nodes.name: Keys
nodes.desc: Superkeys, candidate keys and primary keys, and counting the superkeys of a relation.
nodes.summary: You will be able to identify superkeys, candidate keys and primary keys and count the superkeys of a relation.

nodes.name: Relational algebra
nodes.desc: Selection, projection, product, union, difference and rename, and what queries they express.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write and evaluate relational algebra queries using selection, projection, product, union, difference and rename.

nodes.name: Joins & division
nodes.desc: Natural, theta and outer joins, division for 'for all' queries, and result cardinalities.
nodes.summary: You will be able to use natural, theta and outer joins and division, and compute the cardinality of their results.
topics: Left, right and full outer joins

nodes.name: Relational calculus
nodes.desc: Tuple relational calculus, safe expressions and equivalence with relational algebra.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write tuple relational calculus queries, recognise safe expressions and relate calculus to relational algebra.

nodes.name: SQL
nodes.desc: SELECT–FROM–WHERE, joins, set operations, NULLs, duplicates and constraints in SQL.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write SQL queries with joins, set operations and constraints and predict how NULLs and duplicates behave.

nodes.name: Aggregation & grouping
nodes.desc: Aggregate functions, GROUP BY and HAVING, and how NULLs affect them.
nodes.summary: You will be able to summarise data with aggregate functions, GROUP BY and HAVING and predict how NULLs affect the results.
topics: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN and MAX

nodes.name: Nested queries
nodes.desc: Subqueries with IN, EXISTS, ANY and ALL, correlated subqueries and views.
nodes.summary: You will be able to write and evaluate nested SQL queries using IN, EXISTS, ANY and ALL, correlated subqueries and views.

nodes.name: Functional deps
nodes.desc: FDs, Armstrong's axioms, attribute closure, and equivalence and minimal covers of FD sets.
nodes.summary: You will be able to reason with functional dependencies using Armstrong's axioms, attribute closure and minimal covers.

nodes.name: Finding keys
nodes.desc: Finding all candidate keys from a set of FDs using attribute closure.
nodes.summary: You will be able to find all candidate keys of a relation from its functional dependencies using attribute closure.
topics: Attributes never on the right side

nodes.name: Normalisation
nodes.desc: Redundancy and anomalies, and why we decompose relations.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain how redundancy causes insertion, deletion and update anomalies and why relations are decomposed.

nodes.name: Normal forms
nodes.desc: 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF: testing a relation and identifying its highest normal form.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test relations for 1NF, 2NF, 3NF and BCNF and determine the highest normal form a relation satisfies.
topics: Second normal form and partial dependencies
Third normal form and transitive dependencies

nodes.name: Decomposition
nodes.desc: Lossless-join and dependency-preserving decompositions.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test whether a decomposition is lossless-join and dependency-preserving and decompose into 3NF or BCNF.

nodes.name: Transactions
nodes.desc: ACID properties, transaction states and schedules.
nodes.summary: You will be able to explain ACID properties, transaction states and how transactions interleave in schedules.

nodes.name: Serializability
nodes.desc: Conflict and view serializability, and testing with a precedence graph.
nodes.summary: You will be able to test schedules for conflict and view serializability using precedence graphs.

nodes.name: Recoverable schedules
nodes.desc: Recoverable, cascadeless and strict schedules.
nodes.summary: You will be able to classify schedules as recoverable, cascadeless or strict and explain cascading rollbacks.

nodes.name: Concurrency control
nodes.desc: Two-phase locking and its variants, timestamp ordering and deadlock handling in databases.
nodes.summary: You will be able to apply two-phase locking variants and timestamp ordering and handle deadlocks in database systems.
topics: Timestamp ordering and Thomas write rule

nodes.name: Logging & recovery
nodes.desc: Write-ahead logging, undo and redo, checkpoints and crash recovery.
nodes.summary: You will be able to describe write-ahead logging, undo and redo, checkpoints and how a database recovers after a crash.

nodes.name: File organisation
nodes.desc: Records and blocks, blocking factor, primary, clustering and secondary indexes, multilevel indexes.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute blocking factors and index sizes and compare primary, clustering, secondary and multilevel indexes.

nodes.name: B-trees
nodes.desc: B-tree order, node capacity, height, insertion and splitting.
nodes.summary: You will be able to compute B-tree order, node capacity and height and trace insertion with node splitting.
topics: Minimum and maximum keys per node

nodes.name: B+ trees
nodes.desc: B+ tree indexes: order from block size, insertion with splits, deletion, height and range queries.
nodes.summary: You will be able to size B+ tree indexes from block size and trace insertion, deletion, height and range queries.
topics: Height and number of block accesses
